sections.h2: How does Miami Beach's history shape a house sale today?
sections.html:
The city began as a barrier island joined to the mainland by the Collins Bridge, and it incorporated on March 26, 1915. Hotels, shopping streets and residential neighborhoods followed within a few decades, which is why a Miami Beach street can mix very different buildings.

The city's own history page lists hospitality, retail, technology, healthcare, finance and the arts among its key sectors, and its rental and zoning rules are strict, as the rental section below shows.

  • Pricing: compare your house with sales of the same building type, not the whole city.
  • Rental rules: confirm what a buyer may legally do with the property.
  • Records: collect permits, association documents and insurance history.

sections.h2: What does QuickFacts say about housing and residents here?
sections.html:
The city's land area is 7.69 square miles, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 81,594 residents. The 2020 count was 82,890 and the 2010 count was 87,779, so the population has edged down over a decade.

QuickFacts lists 41,600 households at an average of 1.95 people for 2020 to 2024, with 18.8 percent of residents age 65 or older. Another 81.4 percent of people aged one and over lived in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is modest. Mean travel time to work is 26.7 minutes, and 52.9 percent of adults 25 and over hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Sellers in smaller, older households often face estate sales or downsizing, each with its own paperwork.

sections.h2: Can I use my Miami Beach house as a short-term rental?
sections.html:
Not a single-family house. The Resiliency Code, in sections 7.5.4.13(d)(E) and 7.5.4.11(a), bars rentals of less than six months and one day in all single-family homes and in many multi-family buildings in certain zoning districts.

Rentals that are allowed need a city Business Tax Receipt and a Resort Tax account. City code section 102-386 requires both numbers in every advertisement or listing. The city also publishes a list of apartment buildings authorized for short-term rental, grouped by zoning district.

A buyer who plans nightly stays will check these rules, and so should you. If your past income came from stays the code forbids, expect offers to be priced as a long-term rental or an owner-occupied home. Code Compliance and the city's Customer Service Center take reports of illegal rentals, and the city publishes a zoning map to check a property.

sections.h2: What does a Miami Beach seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade is the one Florida county with its own deed stamp structure: 60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax that does not apply to a deed transferring only a single-family dwelling. Every other county charges 70 cents.

The base is the price plus any mortgage or lien on the property, whether the buyer assumes it or not. The clerk of court takes payment at the moment the deed is recorded.

  • Payoff letters for the mortgage, any home equity line and judgment liens.
  • Unpaid property tax for the year, prorated with the buyer.
  • For condos and co-ops, an estoppel or payoff letter from the association.
  • Title insurance and recording, as set out in the contract.

sections.h2: How do Miami-Dade property tax dates affect a Miami Beach sale?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade's property appraiser sets assessments, and the county's tax collector sends the bills. The appraiser's office says it does not send bills and does not set or collect taxes. It certified the 2026 roll on October 16, 2026.

Florida bills arrive in November. Pay in November and the discount is 4 percent, then 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. After April 1 an unpaid bill is delinquent.

When a homestead sells, the exemption on that parcel ends and the buyer's assessment resets to full just value the next January 1. A seller moving to another Florida home may port the saved assessment amount by filing with the homestead application by March 1.

sections.h2: What if the Miami Beach house is inherited or tenant-occupied?
sections.html:
An heir needs legal authority before a deed can be signed, and Florida's streamlined summary administration is open to estates of $150,000 or less in non-exempt property or to deaths more than two years ago.

A tenant complicates timing. A Florida landlord may serve 3 days' written notice for unpaid rent, excluding weekends and court holidays, and a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice. If a tenant stays past a court judgment, the sheriff posts 24 hours' notice before restoring possession.

Many buyers prefer a vacant house, so decide early whether you will deliver it empty or sell it with the lease in place.

sections.h2: What if I am behind on a Miami Beach mortgage?
sections.html:
Ask the lender for a payoff figure and the case status in writing. When a Florida court enters final judgment, the clerk sells the property between 20 and 35 days later unless the plaintiff agrees to a longer period.

Selling before that sale protects any equity you hold. After a sale, homeowners are told to check with the clerk within 10 days about surplus funds.

sections.h2: Which Miami Beach records should I gather before listing?
sections.html:
Start with the deed, the latest tax bill, any association governing documents and the insurance declarations page. Add permits for roofs, windows, air conditioning and electrical work, since buyers and their lenders tend to ask.

If the property has ever been rented short term, collect the Business Tax Receipt and Resort Tax paperwork. If it was never approved, say so plainly to buyers instead of letting an inspector or the city raise it first.

Check the county's property fraud alert service run by the clerk, which tells an owner within 24 hours when a deed or mortgage is recorded in their name. It is free and takes a few minutes to join.

sections.h2: How do I compare a cash offer with listing in Miami Beach?
sections.html:
Work out what a listing would leave after commission, repairs and carrying costs, and set it beside the written cash figure. The offer should say who pays the stamp tax, the title policy and recording, and what happens to a deposit.

Ask for the settlement date and the closing agent in writing. If the buyer wants to assign the contract to someone else, ask who that person is before you commit.

faqs.q: When did Miami Beach become a city?
faqs.a: The city's history page says Miami Beach incorporated on March 26, 1915, when it was an undeveloped barrier island linked to the mainland by the Collins Bridge.

faqs.q: Is short-term renting allowed in Miami Beach houses?
faqs.a: No for single-family homes. The city prohibits rentals of less than six months and one day there, and allows them only in certain multi-family buildings and zoning districts with a Business Tax Receipt and Resort Tax account.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Miami Beach?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $556,700 for owner-occupied units for 2020 to 2024, a citywide midpoint that may sit far from your own house's value.

faqs.q: What deed stamp tax applies in Miami Beach?
faqs.a: Miami-Dade's rate is 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, and the surtax is not due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling, as the Department of Revenue prints it.

faqs.q: Does my homestead cap pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. A sale is a change of ownership, so the property goes back to just value the following January 1. You can ask the appraiser about portability for a new Florida homestead.
